title: Rabbi Achai, a Fourth-Generation Palestinian Amora
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Achai, a fourth-generation Palestinian Amora.

He is mentioned in Terumot, beginning of chapter 10: Rabbi Hezekiah, Rabbi Achai, in the name of Rabbi Ba bar Mamal; and in Sanhedrin chapter 4, halakhah 7: Rabbi Hezekiah, Rabbi Achi, in the name of Rabbi Abbahu.

Yalkut, Lekh Lekha, on “What will You give me,” has Rabbi Achai and Rabbi Berekhya reporting Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani. Yalkut, Kings I, remez 173, copies Rabbi Achi reporting Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. Perhaps he is Rabbi Achi, who supervised bills of divorce in Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Assi’s time, as in Gittin 5b. Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:8 has Rabbi Ba reporting Rabbi Achi; Eruvin 9:2 has Rabbi Yose reporting Rabbi Achia. He is also mentioned in Ketubot 3:4.

notes.text: Achai, Achi and Achia remain reported spellings. The identification with the supervisor of bills of divorce is tentative. The Shimon ben Gamliel abbreviation does not by itself specify a generation.

The consulted Gittin 5b explicitly names Rabbi Achai, appointed over bills of divorce, followed by Ami and Assi. This supports the named occurrence, not identity with all Achai/Achi/Achia transmissions. Hyman’s fourth-generation placement and tentative identification remain his; the exact Yalkut readings were not independently inspected here.
